page: Amazon Web Services r6g.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by 64-bit ARM architecture. The server features 32 dedicated physical cores running at 2.5 GHz using custom AWS Graviton processors with ARM Neoverse-N1 cores. Hardware multithreading is absent, providing one thread per core for predictable thread isolation. The instance is configured with 256.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-core allocation of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Cache hierarchy includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, backed by hardware-accelerated cryptographic extensions.

Benchmark evaluations show average multi-threaded execution capabilities, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 11647.0 and a multi-core stress-ng result of 48584.84. In-memory data workloads exhibit solid performance, demonstrated by 37.16 million operations per second during Redis SET tests and an uncached large-block read memory bandwidth of 165.0 GB/sec. Conversely, single-threaded processing presents a performance bottleneck, characterized by a Geekbench single-core score of 950.0 and single-threaded gzip compression rates of 20.34 GB/sec. Compilation tasks with Clang and PassMark database metrics both register in the median tier.

The r6g.8xlarge delivers 12 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth but provides no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached volumes for data retention. The system lacks GPU hardware accelerators, which is reflected in below-average LLM token processing speeds. Given its high RAM density and 32 dedicated physical cores, the instance provides qualitative cost efficiency for memory-constrained architectures that distribute concurrency effectively. Recommended workloads include in-memory databases like Redis, mid-sized relational database instances, distributed caches, and multi-threaded batch data processing pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r6g.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro System, powered by 32 dedicated ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 cores clocked at 2.5 GHz. Configured without simultaneous multithreading, it pairs 32 physical cores with 256.0 GB of system memory, delivering an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The instance delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps, contains no bundled local storage, and includes no dedicated graphics hardware. Benchmarks show balanced multi-threaded performance, recording 37.16 million Redis SET operations per second and steady multi-core CPU throughput, while single-core performance remains in the lower quartile. The architecture delivers strong resource density and qualitative hardware cost efficiency for horizontally scaled or multi-threaded memory-heavy services. It is appropriately matched for workloads such as in-memory caches, distributed key-value stores, relational database management systems, and high-throughput web backends that benefit from expansive memory without demanding ultra-high single-thread compute.
